name: Jeremai
overview: Jeremai is a male biblical figure identified as a descendant of Hashum. His unique attribute is that he was connected to a situation involving a foreign wife, as noted in Ezra 10:33. There is no additional information about his tribe or other personal details.
namesAndTitles: The name Jeremai appears once in Scripture and is possibly derived from a root meaning 'fat.' It is a proper name without indication that it was given directly by God, as referenced in Ezra 10:33.
familyAndRelationships: Jeremai is explicitly recorded as a descendant of Hashum. Beyond this, Scripture does not provide further family relationships or connections for him apart from his association with Hashum and the mention of a foreign wife in his lineage.
scriptureSignificance: Jeremai's significance lies primarily in his genealogical role as a descendant of Hashum during the post-exilic period. His mention in Ezra 10:33 highlights the issue of intermarriage with foreign wives among the returned exiles, a matter addressed by Ezra to preserve the covenant community's purity. Thus, Jeremai's record serves as part of the historical account emphasizing faithfulness to God's commands in the restoration era.
